title: +INTRODUCTION TO FOREST ENGINEERING
description: Introduces Forest Engineering and provides the framework for understanding the diverse array of roles and job opportunities available in the forest engineering field. Includes a series of lectures and assignments related to engineering skills and tools, an understanding of scientific method and engineering ethics, and a diverse mix of guest speakers representing recent forest engineering graduates, supplementing the Instructor lectures covering the broad array of job and career opportunities including options related to professional engineering licensing.
registration_restrictions:
Prerequisites: CORE 100*, 300*, BA 100*, 300*, ED 100*, 300*, ENGR 110*, 110H*, 310*, LA 100*, 300*, SCI 100*, 300* or minimum score of 1 in 'Baccalaureate Core Student'.
* May be taken concurrently.
A minimum grade of D- is required in CORE 100, CORE 300, BA 100, BA 300, ED 100, ED 300, ENGR 110, ENGR 110H, ENGR 310, LA 100, LA 300, SCI 100 and SCI 300.

Enrollment limited to students in the following colleges:

  • College of Forestry
  • Pre-Engineering Program
  • Pre-Forestry Program
  • University Exploratory Study
